thread_pair_example: one Fsmooth launch (fine level: 8 boxes of 9^3 nodes, 128-thread blocks): the thread of node (i,j,k) loads sol(i+1,j,k) (L228) while the thread of node (i+1,j,k) stores sol(i+1,j,k) (L86); nodes adjacent in i are adjacent lanes of one warp (intra-warp), nodes adjacent in j/k are in other warps of the block (cross-warp) or, at a 128-thread block boundary, in another block (cross-block). Which relation a detector sees depends on the node's flat index; all three occur in the same launch.
class_reason: All accesses are plain global loads/stores (LDG.E.64 / STG.E.64, no atomics, no fences, no .STRONG) by different threads of one grid in one kernel launch: neighbour loads of sol versus the in-place store to sol of the neighbouring node, with nothing ordering them (a grid has no inter-block ordering inside a launch) -> data race of plain accesses (DR); no strong/atomic access, so no SC component. A true intra-kernel RAW/WAR on one array; the result is nondeterministic.
buggy_expected: The pair is reported as DR on global memory: the L227/L228 (and other L207-L232) loads of sol in mlndlap_adotx_aa versus the L86 store in mlndabeclap_jacobi_aa, both inlined into the Fsmooth lambda, by different threads of the same launch (RAW/WAR on neighbouring nodes).

fixed.reason: The fix removes the Jacobi pair and runs the 2^D-coloured Gauss-Seidel on the GPU too: one ParallelForStrided launch per colour (AMReX_MLNodeABecLaplacian.cpp L142-L150 of the fixed file, multicolor_offset(color), IntVect(2) stride), calling mlndabeclap_gauss_seidel_aa whose stencil loads (AMReX_MLNodeABecLap_3D_K.H L32-L57, x-neighbours at L52/L53) and in-place store (L60, STG.E.64 at 0x1df0 / 0x1c00 in the two instantiations) now only touch nodes of different parity than the node being updated: nodes of one colour differ by >= 2 in at least one coordinate, so they are outside each other's +-1 stencil, and consecutive colour launches are stream-ordered. The same load and store instructions exist in the fixed SASS (it is the same stencil), so absence of a report depends on the detector separating launches / address sets.
